reason: The goal is a stable crane frame, so I'll start by attaching the mast to its base.
expectation: I expect a basic upright frame that can later be braced against sideways bending.

alternatives.reason: The pulley seems useful for lifting, but the frame comes first for the current goal.

effect: The upright mast is in place, so I can now brace the frame against sideways bending.
reaction: A straightforward first step; nothing surprising yet.
reason: Diagonal braces directly address the goal of resisting sideways bending.
expectation: I expect the braces to stiffen the upright mast, though the base may still need attention.

alternatives.reason: The pulley will likely help lift the basket, but bracing is more relevant to the current goal.

effect: The diagonal braces make the mast resist skewing; the boom can now be added to the frame.
reaction: The rectangle-to-diamond explanation makes the braces' purpose clear.
reason: I'll add the boom to continue building the crane's frame.
expectation: I expect the boom to attach to the braced mast, possibly needing its support stay afterward.

alternatives.reason: The pulley is needed for lifting, but I want to finish the frame first.

effect: The hinged boom is attached, and its support stay is now available to fit.
reaction: A straightforward continuation of the frame.
reason: The stay should support the hinged boom, continuing the frame build.
expectation: I expect the stay to hold the boom in position and strengthen its support.

alternatives.reason: The pulley is useful for lifting, but the boom support seems more relevant now.

effect: The boom is now held by its stay; the pulley assembly is the only offered combination.
reason: I'll assemble the pulley because it's the only available action and should help the crane lift.
expectation: I expect the wheel to fit into the fork on its axle, forming a pulley that can be attached to the crane.

effect: The pulley is assembled, and I understand it changes the rope's direction rather than reducing the load.
reaction: The distinction about a fixed pulley is useful and clear.
reason: Attaching the pulley is the only offered combination and advances the crane build.
expectation: I expect the forked pulley to attach to the boom so a rope can run over it.

effect: The pulley is attached at the boom tip; the spreading feet are the remaining offered combination.
reason: I'll add the feet because it's the only offered combination and they should help stabilize the crane.
expectation: I expect the wider feet to make the crane less likely to tip, although I don't know whether that completes the goal.

effect: The spreading feet completed the crane frame; the wider footprint helps stability while the triangular braces resist sideways bending.
reaction: The finished structure ties the parts together, though I was curious to see it lift the basket.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the diagonal braces was most worthwhile: the rectangle-to-diamond explanation made their structural purpose easy to understand.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the boom and its stay felt like straightforward assembly, with little explanation of how the stay works.

surprise.text: The fixed pulley changes the direction of the pull but does not halve the weight; that was a useful distinction.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary, though attaching the pulley was required before completion even though the stated goal concerned resisting sideways bending.

continue.text: I would continue to see the crane lift the basket and learn how the completed frame handles a load. The clear explanations make that prospect interesting.
